script: Josephine Baker was a movie star, and she was also a Nazi-hunting spy nobody suspected. In the 1930s, she was one of the most famous performers in Paris, adored by audiences across Europe. When the Nazis invaded France, French intelligence recruited her precisely because nobody would suspect a celebrity. She smuggled secret messages written in invisible ink on her own sheet music, carried past checkpoints without a single search. She attended parties with Nazi officials, charming them into revealing troop movements and military secrets. Guards waved her through borders because they only saw a famous face, never a spy. For years, she risked execution every single time she crossed a checkpoint smiling. France later awarded her the Legion of Honor and the Croix de Guerre for her service. Josephine Baker was a movie star, and the Nazis never once suspected the spy underneath.
